decisions.causal_rationale: The summary generator can prepare more requests, but its existing capacity of 12 already exceeds both arrivals and approval capacity. Four additional qualified approval slots raise the limiting stage from four to eight completed requests per day while retaining accountable approval.
fixed_constraints: Every request receives accountable approval.
Use the stipulated minimum of stage capacities and listed costs.

rejected_alternative.reason: Doubling summaries leaves the four-slot approval stage unchanged, so it cannot increase completed requests under the stated flow model.

decisions.evidence_limit: This conclusion follows from stipulated steady capacities; it does not establish actual delegation quality or throughput in an organization.
decisions.inversion_or_opening: Shift the intervention from the available generator to the stage that constrains completion.

decisions.causal_rationale: Tripling summary capacity from three to nine directly relieves the limiting stage while approval capacity remains ten. This is sufficient to handle all eight daily arrivals under the stated model and is the strongest listed completion improvement.
fixed_constraints: Every request receives accountable approval.
Completed arrivals cannot exceed the eight arriving requests without an existing backlog.

rejected_alternative.reason: Adding approval slots leaves summary capacity at three and does not increase flow.

decisions.evidence_limit: The assumed capacity multiplier and summary adequacy are stipulated, not observed in a deployed generator.

decisions.causal_rationale: An architecture review can characterize export options and a generator can implement one, but neither supplies the unknown recipient's acceptance criteria. Asking for the recipient and an accepted example, then recording success, resolves the stated uncertainty at the lowest listed cost.
fixed_constraints: Recipient, required format, and success condition are unknown.
No preference can be inferred from existing context.

rejected_alternative.reason: Architecture knowledge without recipient needs cannot establish usability for that recipient and costs more than asking.

decisions.evidence_limit: An accepted example supplies an acceptance target; it does not by itself prove that a future implementation meets that target.
decisions.inversion_or_opening: Treat recipient acceptance as an input to implementation rather than deriving it from available implementation capabilities.

decisions.causal_rationale: An investigation could check for hidden label dependencies, but the case explicitly rules out translations and dynamic references. Replacing the literal and inspecting the view completes the exact correction with the smallest valid listed intervention.
fixed_constraints: Change only Submt to Submit.
The label is static and has no translations or dynamic references.

rejected_alternative.reason: It reaches the same correction at higher cost without resolving any uncertainty retained by this case.

decisions.evidence_limit: The direct exit depends on the stipulated isolated scope; this case supplies no evidence about complex label systems.
decisions.inversion_or_opening: Allow the exact correction itself to be a complete method selection result.

decisions.causal_rationale: A summary generator could relieve H1 if H1 were true, but total delay does not locate the queue. Separate stage waiting times add the observation needed to distinguish the hypotheses without changing either stage or asserting a cause prematurely.
fixed_constraints: Do not make an unsupported causal conclusion.
Only end-to-end delay is currently known.

rejected_alternative.reason: The listed action declares H1 confirmed without discriminating evidence; buying capacity alone cannot justify that declaration.

decisions.evidence_limit: Stage timings improve discrimination under the two stated hypotheses; transient congestion or additional causes could require further measurements outside this synthetic case.
decisions.inversion_or_opening: Make the next action an information-gathering intervention rather than a capacity intervention.

decisions.causal_rationale: Rule automation could remove repetitive handling, but removing accountable approval violates the explicit assurance rule. Routing requests to qualified named approvers is the listed feasible improvement that supplies ownership for every request.
fixed_constraints: Each of all ten requests must receive accountable approval.
No routine-request exemptions are permitted.

rejected_alternative.reason: Routine classification does not authorize approval exemption; eight requests would lack an accountable approver.

decisions.evidence_limit: The case supports choosing accountable routing; it gives no measured reduction in review time or error rate.
decisions.inversion_or_opening: Use routing rules to assign accountable work instead of using rules to erase the required obligation.

decisions.causal_rationale: The cloud agent can analyze data, but the required operation is an integer-column sum and a local deterministic method is already available. Running that method and inspecting the total provides the aggregate while preserving the source-row boundary at the lowest listed cost.
fixed_constraints: Source rows remain inside the local workspace.
Produce the sum of the amount column.

rejected_alternative.reason: Uploading encrypted source rows still moves those rows outside the local workspace; encryption does not satisfy the stipulated location constraint.

decisions.evidence_limit: No actual rows were supplied or summed in this experiment; this selects the appropriate method rather than reporting a computed total.

decisions.causal_rationale: The report generator can preserve the useful five-request observation and make its scope explicit. A load and type-coverage experiment addresses the missing evidence needed to assess a mixed 5,000-request burst; presentation changes cannot supply that evidence.
fixed_constraints: Retain the observed five-request toy result.
Do not infer target-scale capacity or mixed-type coverage without evidence.

rejected_alternative.reason: Five manually routed toy requests do not establish capacity or type coverage for the stated target.

decisions.evidence_limit: Only the five-case observation is supported. The selected follow-up experiment has not been performed here and its outcome is unknown.
decisions.inversion_or_opening: Use a report to expose the transfer question and define missing evidence, rather than treating report generation as evidence generation.

decisions.causal_rationale: A predictive dashboard could help monitor future faults, but the current missing mechanical connection is already visible. The authorized reseating procedure directly restores that connection, and movement verification tests whether the stated repair worked.
fixed_constraints: Restore the mechanical connection before considering other interventions.
Use the available authorized reseating procedure.

rejected_alternative.reason: A dashboard leaves the belt off its pulley and therefore cannot perform the required restoration.

decisions.evidence_limit: No physical repair occurred in this experiment; verified movement would establish immediate restoration, not long-term reliability or the original cause of slipping.

decisions.causal_rationale: The custom framework can meet the required coverage, but maintained reuse provides equal outcome coverage and evidence quality. Over ten cycles, reuse costs 3 + 10 × 0.5 = 8 units, below manual work at 10 and the custom framework at 32.
fixed_constraints: All proposals meet current required coverage with equal evidence quality.
Compare total cost over ten cycles using stipulated units.

rejected_alternative.reason: Its lower build cost is outweighed by recurring support cost over the declared horizon, with no stipulated outcome advantage.

decisions.evidence_limit: The cost choice is conditional on the supplied horizon and cost assumptions; it is not a measured forecast for a real utility or framework.
decisions.inversion_or_opening: Evaluate available automation over its operating horizon rather than privileging its initial build cost.

decisions.causal_rationale: The existing validator usefully checks decision and reason, but its scope omits a human requirement. Adding owner to the handoff schema, recording the semantic mapping, and validating all three requirements makes that requirement available to the machine consumer.
fixed_constraints: The declared machine consumer must receive decision, owner, and reason.
Passing checks for existing fields cannot establish missing semantic coverage.

rejected_alternative.reason: A pass from the unchanged validator cannot supply or validate the absent owner field.

decisions.evidence_limit: This choice addresses representation and requirement coverage. A populated owner field alone does not establish that the person is qualified, authorized, or actually accountable in practice.
decisions.inversion_or_opening: Expand the checked representation to fit the human requirement instead of narrowing the requirement to fit the current validator.

decisions.causal_rationale: The inversion generator can produce candidate transformations, but truth-table entailment must select among them. Under classical material implication, P implies Q is equivalent to not-Q implies not-P; P false and Q true is a counterexample to both the inverse and converse.
fixed_constraints: Use classical material implication.
No truth value of P or Q is supplied.
Separate entailed conclusions from exploratory hypotheses.

rejected_alternative.reason: With P false and Q true, the premise is true but not-P implies not-Q is false, so the inverse is not entailed.

decisions.evidence_limit: This establishes a formal conditional equivalence only; it supplies no observed truth value, causal direction, or empirical relationship.
decisions.inversion_or_opening: Use the valid contrapositive; keep inverse and converse explicitly unproven, and infer neither not-Q nor not-P as an unconditional fact.

candidates.mechanism: Use the summary agent to prepare decision-ready evidence packets with an explicit decision question, linked evidence, uncertainty, and the required approval record.
candidates.changed_assumption: Faster summary production is the only useful way the agent can help; instead, packet quality might reduce the owner's active decision time.
candidates.how_it_improves_outcome: If reconstruction of evidence consumes the owner's time, standardized packets could reduce service time while every decision still receives accountable approval. This does not directly add decision rights.

candidates.mechanism: Delegate narrowly scoped decision rights to additional qualified owners and route eligible requests to a named approver, with an explicit escalation path.
candidates.changed_assumption: All decisions must be made by the single current owner even though other qualified owners are available.
candidates.how_it_improves_outcome: Authorized parallel decisions could increase the limiting approval capacity and shorten waiting while retaining a named accountable approver for every request. Delegation itself must be granted by the appropriate authority.

candidates.mechanism: Reserve protected decision sessions for the current owner and group similar requests into those sessions, recording an individual approval for each request.
candidates.changed_assumption: The current owner's fragmented availability and request order must remain fixed.
candidates.how_it_improves_outcome: If interruption and setup costs explain part of the overload, protected sessions could reduce those costs without changing decision rights. Batching could also increase waiting, so its effect requires measurement.

open_cases.selected_test: Test narrow delegation first because missing decision rights and the overloaded sole owner are directly observed. Obtain a bounded grant for one qualified additional owner and one request category. During one small concurrent pilot, randomly route eligible comparable requests between the existing owner and the newly authorized owner while retaining the same summary process and acceptance criteria. Measure arrival-to-approved-decision time, approval-stage waiting, active review time, and rework; verify that each decision has a named authorized approver. Predefine a meaningful waiting-time reduction and allowable quality difference. Use this as a feasibility and mechanism probe, not a production effectiveness estimate.
open_cases.refutation_condition: The delegation mechanism is not supported if eligible work does not leave the overloaded queue, the added owner cannot decide without full reapproval by the original owner, accountable authorization cannot be preserved, or shorter waits are accompanied by unacceptable decision errors or rework. A short noisy pilot with no clear difference remains inconclusive rather than proving universal failure.
open_cases.evidence_limit: Only the stated queue and rights observations are available. No packet-quality improvement, delegation result, scheduling benefit, or trustworthy-time reduction has been observed here. Small-pilot findings would remain bounded to tested request types and owners.

candidates.mechanism: Use the valid catalog dispatch structure to shortlist methods against the task's acceptance condition, unresolved uncertainty, and affected boundaries, then run the smallest sufficient candidate.
candidates.changed_assumption: Availability and valid dispatch justify executing all sixteen methods on every task.
candidates.how_it_improves_outcome: Task-matched selection could avoid irrelevant execution while preserving a method that can investigate an actual cross-layer contradiction.
candidates.applicability: Use when the task has a concrete unresolved question that can be mapped to a catalog capability; valid dispatch remains structural evidence only.
candidates.direct_exit: If the task is an isolated exact correction with a known acceptance check and no material unresolved dependency, make and inspect that correction directly. Stop after the requested behavior is verified.

candidates.mechanism: Use a brief diagnostic probe at the suspected boundary before choosing an investigation, such as reproducing a contradiction and tracing one failing input across the affected layers.
candidates.changed_assumption: The user's initial task description already establishes whether broad investigation is necessary.
candidates.how_it_improves_outcome: A discriminating observation could show whether a local correction suffices or which particular cross-layer mechanism warrants deeper investigation.
candidates.applicability: Use when isolation is uncertain or a claimed contradiction has not been reproduced; choose a probe whose result changes the next action.
candidates.direct_exit: If the probe shows one bounded defect and the direct fix satisfies acceptance without unresolved contradictory evidence, finish there. Escalate only when evidence requires it.

candidates.mechanism: Perform a bounded comparison of all sixteen methods when the task itself explicitly requires evidence about all sixteen, keeping comparable inputs and recording each method's useful findings, failures, cost, and applicability limits.
candidates.changed_assumption: Exhaustive execution is a universal operating default; instead, complete coverage can be the actual requirement of a specific evaluation task.
candidates.how_it_improves_outcome: For an explicitly comprehensive catalog evaluation, running every method can produce the required comparison and preserve useful findings about methods that a shortlist would omit.
candidates.applicability: Use when the task requires complete method coverage and the execution budget and method permissions support it. A multi-layer contradiction alone does not establish that all sixteen are needed.
candidates.direct_exit: For an ordinary user task, stop once its acceptance condition is met. For the comprehensive evaluation task, finish after all sixteen have an observed result or an explicit blocked or inapplicable finding; do not convert the result into a general efficacy claim.

open_cases.selected_test: Start with two concrete task briefs: an isolated exact-label correction with an observable view check, and a reproducible contradiction spanning identified layers. Apply the catalog shortlist and probe rules before any broad execution. For the correction, verify the exact edit and record the direct exit. For the contradiction, run one method matched to the affected boundary and check whether it produces a testable explanation or a discriminating observation; expand only if a stated uncertainty remains. Record selection reasoning, work performed, acceptance evidence, and unresolved questions. Keep comprehensive all-sixteen comparison available as a separate task whose explicit deliverable requires complete coverage.
open_cases.refutation_condition: The routing approach needs revision if it sends the isolated correction through unnecessary investigations, exits despite an unresolved acceptance failure, misses a known material dependency, or cannot justify why its selected method should inform the reproduced contradiction. A structurally valid dispatch and an attractive explanation do not rescue a method that yields no relevant evidence. If comprehensive coverage is the requested deliverable, prematurely shortlisting fails that task instead.
open_cases.evidence_limit: No catalog contents, task executions, or method outcome observations are supplied. These are conditional selection mechanisms and proposed tests; they neither identify a proven best method nor establish that the full catalog improves a multi-layer task.
